newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech utility EOP sees lower 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Czech utility EOP sees lower 1996 net.

text.p: Czech utility Elektrarny Opatovice (EOP) a.s. said on Wednesday it expected to post a 1996 net profit of 520 million crowns, according to preliminary figures, down from 535 million the previous year.
It added that revenues in 1996 totalled 3.371 billion crowns, down from 4.234 billion in 1995.
"The lower profit figure is due to lower electricity prices for consumers (in 1996) than in 1995," said Zdenek Kosar from the firm's press department.
He added that in 1996 EOP supplied consumers with 1,728 gigawatt hours (GWh) of electricity, up from 1,410 GWh in 1995, and 6,151 terrajoules (TJ) of heat, against 5,449 TJ the previous year.
The firm's main shareholders include investment funds SPIF Cesky (19.5 percent) and IPF Komercni Banka (14 percent), as well as Komercni Banka (9.9 percent).
